mission.title: Celebrating excellence
mission.description: At AlayaCare, we believe technology is only as powerful as the changemakers who use it. The Home-Based Care Momentum Awards celebrate the human side of innovation — the late-night visits, the quiet acts of advocacy, and the everyday problem-solving that moves home-based care forward. By participating, you help:
items: Shine a spotlight on unsung heroes: Give frontline caregivers, operational champions, and leaders the recognition they deserve — not just inside your organization, but across the industry.
Share stories that inspire real change: Turn powerful moments of care into stories others can learn from, helping to raise the bar for what great home-based care looks like.

Build momentum for your organization and your teams: Boost morale, pride, and engagement by celebrating contributions that improve outcomes, streamline operations, and transform client and staff experience.
Elevate your brand as a leader in care: Show clients, families, staff, and partners that you’re serious about driving the future of home-based care.

aboutAwards.title: About the awards
aboutAwards.intro1: The Home-Based Care Momentum Awards, presented by AlayaCare, recognize the individuals driving meaningful impact across home-based care in North America.
aboutAwards.intro2: From frontline caregivers to operational leaders, executives, and innovators, this program celebrates the people behind better outcomes, stronger teams, and smarter systems.
aboutAwards.poweredBy1: <link>AlayaCare</link> is a global technology platform purpose-built for home and community-based care. We partner with care organizations to improve outcomes and strengthen the caregiver experience.
aboutAwards.poweredBy2: The Momentum Awards are open to individuals employed by eligible home-based care organizations delivering services in home or community settings, including home care, home health, hospice, home infusion, and related services.
aboutAwards.poweredBy3: This is more than recognition. It's a platform to spotlight the people shaping the future of home-based care, and to build momentum that lifts the entire industry.

hero.title: Eligibility details
hero.subtitle: The Home-Based Care Momentum Awards recognize outstanding individuals who are elevating home-based care every day — from the front lines to the back office, and the C-suite to visionary innovators.
hero.note: All categories share the same organization-level eligibility and then have individual eligibility by category.

organizationLevel.title: Organization-level eligibility (all categories)
organizationLevel.employment: Be currently employed (full-time, part-time, or contract) by a home-based care organization that provides one or more of the following services:

services.adjacentServices: Adjacent or supporting services within home-based care

organizationLevel.setting: Provide services in a home or community-based setting (not exclusively facility-based).

additionalNotes.title: Additional notes
additionalNotes.nominations: Nominations may come from colleagues, supervisors, direct reports, or self-nominations, subject to the award program's submission process.
additionalNotes.oneCategory: Each individual can be nominated in one primary category that best reflects their role and impact.
additionalNotes.multipleNominations: Organizations may submit multiple nominations across categories.
additionalNotes.discretion: Final eligibility and category placement are at the discretion of the awards committee, based on the information provided in the nomination.

categoryLevel.title: Category eligibility
categoryLevel.intro: Each category has specific eligibility requirements. Review the details below to determine the best category for your nomination.
categoryLevel.meetOrganizationLevel: Meet the organization-level eligibility outlined above.

frontline.name: Changemakers in Frontline Care
frontline.description: This category celebrates caregivers who deliver direct care and support in the home or community.

requirements.impact: Positively impact client outcomes, safety, experience, or quality of life through their day-to-day work — creating momentum one visit, one interaction, and one family at a time.
requirements.role: Work in a direct care / client-facing role, such as:
roles: Personal Support Worker (PSW), Home Health Aide (HHA), Home Support Worker (HSW), Care Aide, Companion, or similar
Registered Nurse (RN), Licensed/Registered Practical Nurse (LPN/RPN), Nurse Practitioner (NP)
Allied health professionals providing care at home (e.g., physiotherapist, occupational therapist, speech-language pathologist, social worker, respiratory therapist)
requirements.provide: Provide hands-on care, support, or clinical services in clients' homes or community settings.
requirements.demonstrate: Demonstrate exceptional compassion, reliability, and client-centred care, going above and beyond typical expectations.

operational.name: Changemakers in Operational Excellence
operational.description: This category recognizes behind-the-scenes champions whose work keeps home-based care running smoothly, efficiently, and safely.

requirements.champion: Champion collaboration across teams to solve operational challenges and sustain momentum.
requirements.role: Work in a non-frontline, operations-focused role, such as:
roles: Scheduler, Service Coordinator, Intake Coordinator, Client Services Representative
Operations, Quality, or Performance Improvement Specialist
HR, Finance, Billing, or Payroll professional focused on home-based care
IT Specialist, Systems Administrator, Data/Reporting Analyst, or similar
requirements.playRole: Play a key role in supporting caregivers, clients, and field operations (e.g., scheduling, capacity optimization, workflow design, billing integrity, compliance).

executive.name: Changemakers in Executive Leadership
executive.description: This category honours senior leaders who are shaping the future of home-based care through strategic vision, culture-building, and bold decision-making.

requirements.trackRecord: A track record of setting a strategic direction that builds sustained momentum for their organization and the broader sector.
requirements.role: Hold a senior leadership role at a home-based care organization, typically VP level or above, such as:
roles: Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Chief Operating Officer (COO), Chief Clinical Officer (CCO), Chief Nursing Officer (CNO), Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Chief Strategy Officer (CSO), or equivalent
requirements.responsibility: Have direct or shared responsibility for organizational strategy, growth, quality, or innovation in home-based care services.
demonstrations: Visionary leadership in expanding or improving home-based care
A clear commitment to care quality, safety, and equity
Investment in people and culture (e.g., supporting staff, enabling teams with tools and training, driving engagement)
Tangible impact on organizational performance, client outcomes, or community reach

impact.name: Changemakers in Impact and Innovation
impact.description: This category recognizes trailblazers at any level or function who are driving meaningful change, testing new ideas, or redefining what's possible in home-based care.

requirements.embody: Embody the spirit of a changemaker by turning ideas into action, and action into lasting momentum.
requirements.role: Work in any role or level (frontline, operational, clinical, technical, or leadership) within an eligible home-based care organization.
requirements.leading: Be leading or significantly contributing to unique, high-impact initiatives, for example:
initiatives: Implementing new models of care (e.g., hybrid virtual/in-person care, specialized programs for complex populations)
Piloting or scaling innovative technologies or data-driven approaches that improve client or staff experience
Designing novel workflows, partnerships, or community programs that increase access to care
Advancing equity, inclusion, or culturally competent care in home and community settings
Championing sustainability or scalable best practices that others in the industry can learn from
impacts: The broader home-based care industry (e.g., thought leadership, advocacy, knowledge-sharing)

eligibility.title: Eligibility
eligibility.p1: The Home-Based Care Momentum Awards are open to individuals and organizations operating in the home-based care sector in Canada and the United States. This includes home health, home care, home infusion, hospice, community care, and related services.
eligibility.p2: Nominees must be actively working in the sector at the time of nomination.

nominations.title: Nominations
nominations.p1: Nominations may be submitted by peers, colleagues, organizations, or by self-nomination, unless otherwise stated. All information submitted must be accurate and complete to the best of the nominator's knowledge.
nominations.p2: AlayaCare reserves the right to verify nomination details and request additional information where required.

selection.title: Selection process
selection.p1: Award recipients are selected through a combination of voting and evaluation by a judging panel, as determined by AlayaCare.
selection.p2: Voting is one input into the overall selection process and does not solely determine award recipients. AlayaCare reserves the right to validate votes and take reasonable steps to ensure the integrity of the process. This may include limiting votes, removing duplicate or automated submissions, and excluding votes that appear to be manipulated or inconsistent with the intent of the awards.
selection.p3: The judging panel reviews nominations using established criteria, which may include leadership, impact, influence, innovation, and contribution to advancing home-based care.
selection.p4: Final selections are made at the discretion of AlayaCare, informed by both voting outcomes and judge evaluations. All decisions are final, and no correspondence will be entered into regarding selection outcomes.

useOfContent.title: Use of submitted content
useOfContent.p1: By submitting a nomination or participating in the awards process, nominators and nominees grant AlayaCare a non-exclusive, royalty-free right to use submitted names, quotes, biographies, images, and supporting materials for award-related purposes. This includes promotional, editorial, marketing, and event-related use, in any medium, without additional compensation.

publicity.title: Publicity
publicity.p1: Award recipients agree to participate in reasonable promotional activities related to the awards. This may include interviews, written profiles, social media mentions, or event participation.
publicity.p2: If a nominee does not wish to be publicly recognized, this must be communicated to AlayaCare prior to final selection.

privacy.title: Privacy and marketing communications
privacy.p1: By submitting a nomination, voting, or otherwise participating in the awards, nominators, nominees, and voters consent to the collection and use of their personal information for the administration of the awards.
privacy.p2: In accordance with Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL) and U.S. CAN-SPAM regulations, participants also consent to receiving electronic communications from AlayaCare related to award updates, events, industry insights, content, products, and services relevant to home-based care.
privacy.p3: Participants may withdraw consent and opt out of marketing communications at any time by using the unsubscribe mechanism included in such communications or by contacting AlayaCare directly.
privacy.p4: Personal information will be handled in accordance with applicable Canadian and U.S. privacy laws.

disqualification.title: Disqualification
disqualification.p1: AlayaCare reserves the right to disqualify any nomination or participant if information provided is false, misleading, incomplete, or submitted in violation of these terms and conditions.

changes.title: Changes and cancellation
changes.p1: AlayaCare reserves the right to modify award categories, criteria, timelines, or these terms and conditions at any time. AlayaCare may suspend or cancel the awards if circumstances require, without liability.

governingLaw.title: Governing law
governingLaw.p1: These terms and conditions are governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which AlayaCare operates, without regard to conflict of law principles.
